text:
The dynamics between Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy serve as the primary vehicle for Jane Austen’s exploration of social class and personal growth. Their initial mutual disdain, rooted in Darcy’s pride and Elizabeth’s prejudice, illustrates how societal barriers and personal flaws can obscure true understanding. As they navigate these obstacles, their gradual shift toward respect and love demonstrates the transformative power of self-reflection and the ability to overcome rigid social expectations. This evolution underscores the theme that genuine connection requires looking beyond surface-level judgments and class distinctions.
